cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What is the determinism and discovery split?
cards.answer: A compound AI system should route work by what it demands: exactness-valued, expensive-to-unwind work goes to a deterministic tool that only does what it's told; work whose value is finding something unspecified goes to an agent permitted to be wrong; recurring agent behavior gets demoted into a rule.

cards.heading: Key mechanism
cards.question: When a model repeatedly fumbles the same mechanical task (e.g. the same join or lookup), what is the correction?
cards.answer: Not a better prompt — demote the behavior into a parametrised query, runbook, or rule of thumb the agent invokes, keeping discovery capacity intact while making the mechanical part exact.

cards.heading: Routing criterion
cards.question: What criterion decides whether a task gets a deterministic tool or an agent?
cards.answer: Consequence and reversibility — e.g. a refund or funds transfer gets a deterministic tool plus human approval, because a confident wrong answer there is a loss, not a lead.

cards.heading: Why tolerate wrongness
cards.question: Why is tolerating agent wrongness sometimes valuable, per this rule?
cards.answer: An agent allowed to be wrong occasionally produces an answer nobody would have specified; restricting it to only pre-programmed branches forecloses that discovery entirely.

cards.heading: Under-tooling hazard
cards.question: What hazard does giving a model too little tool access create?
cards.answer: A model with nothing exact to call will reason its way to a plausible-sounding number instead of getting the right one — under-tooling is a hazard in itself.
